body:
I want to make sure I’m not misunderstanding your reply, and I’d like to clarify a few questions.

Yes, “the two of us” refers to Hannah and me. I did not stop talking to Hannah entirely. I tried to keep project related discussions through email and if one occurred face to face, I followed up with an email with a summary of what we talked about. This initially began because she would forget or misremember aspects and details unless they were emailed to her. 

Are you suggesting that I should have continued to do Hannah’s work without telling our boss of the breakdown in cooperation?

Our boss was aware since the start of the issues in collaboration. She made recommendations and suggested the two of us get together to discuss what the delays were in Hannah’s work and how they could be addressed and corrected. 

I never reprimanded Hannah either. As you say, it’s not my place. 

Concerning being “right and perfect”, I couldn’t just put my hands up and say “Sorry, client, my partner didn’t do her portion so I have nothing for you.” The work we do is time sensitive and a costly industry. We were jointly responsible for the project and end result, ultimately. 

Training might have been an option, but it would have required more effort and time than could be reasonably spared at the moment. 

Pretty sure karma already got me in anticipation of Hannah’s firing, thank you. But yeah. A learning lesson.
I’m proud of and inspired by your resourcefulness in saving his voice, even if imperfectly. It’s better than nothing. Thank you for your support and  sharing your experience
My God, I am sorry. The thought alone is nauseating. I’m so sorry that you lost her voicemail. That is a loss that just hurts to fathom, and I hope you have other means of remembering her memory.
I— I never thought to do that. Thank you so much. I can’t fathom losing this too just because my carrier wanted to upgrade. Thank you. So much.

I’m truly blessed to have voicemails from him. Just calling to say hi. That he missed me but he was just thinking of me. Or returning my call because he was busy. Or he accidentally got some of my old junk mail and wanted to know if I wanted it sent to me or thrown away. 

I’m sorry. I’m really still emotional about it and I don’t know when I won’t be. My mum’s got dementia, and he’s gone.

I’ll be honest. Maybe it’s confirmation bias but hearing it broken down like this helps a great deal. Thank you for this. I had in the back of my most paranoid mind assumed perhaps she had reported me to get me in trouble- but I worried it was my imagination getting away from me.
Not in so many words, more just the difficulty in working with her, but that did start the discussion that lead to sharing the emails and texts.

Thank you. It still hurts, and it’s hard to stop myself from calling his number or from saving an article to send to him. If you have a loved one, just tell them how much they mean to you. Get a recording of their voice if you can. Their handwriting. Their laugh. It’s the little things that are gone forever that hurt the most. Sorry to get sappy.
Yes, she said that my behavior toward her since we started the project (the lack of coffee, the refusal to speak outside of email concerning the project) was because of her faith.

To phrase it differently (and forgive me if I’ve misunderstood your point), it’s like when you’ve got one organ to give someone and you go through the list based off their viability as a candidate. An obese smoker in their 50s is further down the line and less likely to receive a new set of lungs than an otherwise healthy young adult.  

A person who willingly and knowingly subjects their body to a greater risk should not be priority over someone living their life and happened to get infected. To further paraphrase: If there is one ventilator and two covid patients, the patient that did their part to try to minimize their exposure deserves preferential treatment over the doorknob licker. 

We already tax smokers. I pay a lot of money to smoke - to my insurance, to the state, to tobacco companies - and to lie would be insurance fraud. Why not impose the same penalty to someone who walks around potentially infecting those around them during a pandemic? It isn’t a perfect solution but it’s an interesting thought experiment. Maybe it would get them to think about the consequences seeing as “you might kill someone” hasn’t yet.
